summary.headline: PNC Infratech FY26 standalone revenue fell to INR 4,633 crore; management guides ~30% growth to INR 6,000 crore in FY27 with ~12% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR 1,458 crore with 12.02% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 100 crore, while FY26 standalone revenue of INR 4,633 crore was below earlier expectations due to delayed appointed dates on four projects worth over INR 4,400 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 6,000 crore (~30% growth), FY28 about 25% higher, and EBITDA near 12% in FY27, citing bitumen and crude-driven cost pressure partly offset by new escalation mechanisms. The company has an unexecuted order book above INR 22,000 crore, and it is diversifying into solar, BESS, coal mining and water. Net surplus on a standalone basis was INR 327 crore, while consolidated net debt to equity was 0.76 times.

segments.name: Highways (HAM/EPC/BOT)
segments.commentary: Four delayed projects (three NHAI, one MPRDC) worth over INR 4,400 crore drove lower FY26 turnover; 14 HAM projects with aggregate bid cost above INR 17,200 crore, 5 at PCOD/COD and 6 under construction.

segments.name: Water (Jal Jeevan Mission, irrigation)
segments.commentary: About INR 300 crore received in FY26 from state payments; FY27 revenue target INR 750 crore. Andhra irrigation: INR 380 crore work done to 31 March, ~INR 700 crore remaining, FY27 target ~INR 200 crore.

segments.name: Coal mining (MDO/item-rate EPC)
segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,956 crore over five years; FY26 turnover ~INR 68 crore; FY27 target ~INR 400 crore and FY28 ~INR 600 crore. Capex of ~INR 350 crore, of which ~INR 250 crore spent in FY26.

segments.name: Solar and BESS
segments.commentary: Order of ~INR 2,000 crore in development; physical execution to start Q3 FY27 after PPA with NHPC. Revenue target INR 600 crore in FY27 and INR 1,400 crore in FY28; equity requirement ~INR 400 crore, ~INR 120 crore in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue guided at ~30% growth to ~INR 6,000 crore; FY28 ~25% growth to ~INR 7,500 crore.
FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at ~12%; FY28 margin to be shared later, expected ~12% if commodity prices normalise.
FY27 new order inflow target ~INR 15,000 crore (INR 3,957 crore highways secured so far, plus ~INR 2,000 crore solar); 60-70% targeted from highways.
FY27 capex target INR 150 crore; interest cost expected to fall INR 3-4 crore from current quarter.
Equity infusion for HAM projects: INR 542 crore remaining over two years, ~INR 350 crore in FY27; internal accruals expected to cover it.
Revenue targets: Varanasi-Kolkata packages INR 1,600-1,800 crore; Jalna-Nanded and Pune Ring Road INR 1,500-1,600 crore; Haryana Orbital Rail balance ~INR 360 crore to FY27/FY28.
capex_capacity: Coal mining capex ~INR 350 crore, ~INR 250 crore spent in FY26; FY27 company capex target INR 150 crore.
Solar: land identified, connectivity in-principle approval received, final approval expected in 1.5-2 months; physical execution from Q3 FY27 after PPA with NHPC.
HAM equity: INR 1,623 crore total requirement (excluding two new HAMs awaiting LOA); INR 1,081 crore infused to March 2026.
Western Bhopal HAM: appointed date expected by end-September 2026 after alignment change; ~INR 100 crore FY27 revenue assumed.
Two new NHAI HAM projects in UP (bid cost INR 3,483 crore combined): appointed date expected in Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded 3,124 km in FY26, over 30% below the 4,500 km target; management expects awarding to improve but timing uncertain.
EPC competition described as cutthroat; management sees less competition in larger HAM and BOT-Toll projects, citing reduced bidder numbers on two recent HAM wins of about INR 1,700 crore each.
Company submitted 15 EPC bids and one HAM bid worth ~INR 14,000 crore; price bids expected to open before end-May and in June.

MoRTH cost escalation mechanism from 1 April 2026 for EPC/HAM/PBMC projects with monthly price adjustment (earlier three months); management expects revised authority cost or extended compensation for new tenders.
Back-to-back pass-through: SPV inflation indices (WPI/CPI) and bitumen price compensation flow to EPC contractor per management.
Vertis Infrastructure Trust: entire payment for the 12-asset divestment received, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY27 and FY28 revenue and margins be viewed given the FY26 shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided ~30% growth to ~INR 6,000 crore in FY27 and ~25% in FY28 (~INR 7,500 crore), with ~12% EBITDA in FY27; some margin pressure expected in Q1-Q2 from bitumen and crude costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the INR 6,000 crore guidance between approved and pending projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance excludes new orders; based on awarded projects with appointed dates, except Western Bhopal (~INR 100 crore assumed) and only 30% of the INR 2,000 crore solar order (INR 600 crore) is included.

qa_highlights.question: Will diversification into new segments hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no cross-subsidy effect is expected; earlier target was 13-13.5% EBITDA, now guided ~12% across the mix, with water and irrigation earlier delivering similar margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on the Varanasi-Kolkata packages and Haryana Orbital Rail?
qa_highlights.answer: Varanasi-Kolkata: INR 336 crore revenue in FY26, INR 1,600-1,800 crore targeted in FY27, no obstructions. Haryana Orbital Rail: over INR 400 crore done (53%), balance ~INR 360 crore to be executed in FY27-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost outlook and what drove the Q4 jump to INR 30 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 rise was from working capital utilisation and term loan interest on machine financing; management expects a reduction of INR 3-4 crore from the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company bid for BOT-Toll projects and how will asset monetisation proceed?
qa_highlights.answer: No BOT-Toll bid submitted yet; evaluating NHAI BOT-Toll opportunities and direct bidding is planned. Monetisation of the five PCOD assets is under evaluation; no framework announced.

risks_watch: Bitumen and fuel cost volatility from West Asia tensions; margin pressure expected in near term before escalation benefits fully flow.
Appointed-date delays (Western Bhopal, two new HAMs expected Q4 FY27, MPRDC) could push FY27 revenue below INR 6,000 crore.
Solar revenue (INR 600 crore FY27) depends on 30% land possession, PPA with NHPC and final approvals.
Receivables: total debtors INR 1,660 crore including HAM INR 372 crore and water INR 868 crore; JJM and Andhra irrigation depend on state payments.
Order inflow: FY27 target ~INR 15,000 crore depends on price-bid opening and NHAI awarding pace; 15 EPC and one HAM bids worth ~INR 14,000 crore pending.
Consolidated net debt to equity of 0.76x and rising working-capital-linked interest cost.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term order pipeline and guidance, but cautious on margins and timing, with repeated caveats tied to commodity volatility and appointed-date timing. Management acknowledged that past guidance was optimistic and some answers on monetisation and FY28 margins were deferred.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 standalone revenue ~30% to ~INR 6,000 crore and FY28 ~25% to ~INR 7,500 crore, with ~12% EBITDA margin; backing is a INR 22,000+ crore order book, two new UP HAMs (appointed date Q4 FY27), solar execution from Q3 FY27 and coal ramp to ~INR 400 crore, but NHAI awarding was 30% below target and FY26 revenue fell ~20%.
